thread:
deploy-bot: runtime-detect: policy=NO_SUID_IN_CONTAINER severity=high namespace=payments pod=payments-worker-5 container=worker image=registry.internal/redwood/payments@sha256:abcd1234 added=/usr/bin/.suid_helper (suid) :bangbang:
elena: :eyes: got the alert. What node is that on? can we isolate?
raj: node: gke-payments-pool-3-7c9b (10.12.45.22). I see a matching falco event in stack.
marcos: copying logs + kernel events now. pulling pod exec for ls -la /usr/bin and ps aux.
elsena: typo — elena: thanks. steps: 1) cordon node 2) scale down replica set to 0 for payments-worker 3) collect container fs tar and image manifest 4) check recent image pushes and registry audit 5) check RBAC, KMS access 6) open incident ticket.
raj: cordoning now: `kubectl cordon gke-payments-pool-3-7c9b`
sara-sre: I started a drain with `kubectl drain gke-payments-pool-3-7c9b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — will stop new pods landing.
marcos: mounted the container and confirmed file present, owner=root, mode=4755. suspicious. grabbing tar:
```
kubectl exec -n payments payments-worker-5 -c worker -- tar -czf /tmp/fs-snapshot.tar.gz /usr/bin/.suid_helper /etc/passwd || true
kubectl cp payments/payments-worker-5:/tmp/fs-snapshot.tar.gz ./fs-snapshot-payments-worker-5.tar.gz
```
marcos: saved sha256 of file: df3b2a9c... adding to ticket.
elena: audit-bot, fetch registry push logs for that image digest and last 24h of auth events for the payments service account used by the CI pipeline.
audit-bot: registry: found push by ci-service-account@redwood-ci 2026-01-18T03:12:48Z, image tag v1.3.4 -> sha256:abcd1234. no other pushes in 24h. auth: ci-service-account used token exchange at 2026-01-18T03:11:53Z from runners-redwood-5.
elena: good. check KMS: did any decrypt/encrypt requests happen for key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/container-keys in the same timeframe?
audit-bot: KMS: 2 decrypt calls by payments-service-sa@project-id at 2026-01-18T03:12:49Z and 03:12:51Z from IP 34.120.8.22 (GKE node).
raj: where did the suid file come from? could be buildpack, or post-start script. check Dockerfile and entrypoint in registry.
marcos: pulled image filesystem layers locally with `skopeo` and diffed layers. Layer added the file at layer index 4, created 2026-01-18T03:12:47Z. That matches CI pipeline time.
elsena: ok possible CI compromise or bad build step. check who had permission to update CI service account or decouple KMS key. Check IAM changes.
raj: checking IAM audit logs for service account key creation or role binding changes in last 7d.
marcos: also noticing container had CAP_SYS_ADMIN removed but had CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE present — odd but not enough to create suid; suid binary means it was baked into image or injected via a writeable layer.
elsena: next: 1) snapshot registry layer + upload to secure analysis bucket 2) rotate any CI credentials that could have pushed (short-term revoke tokens) 3) lock the image tag v1.3.4 in deployment to a known good digest 4) run full vulnerability scan on registry image 5) notify product/security stakeholders, escalate to incident.
sara-sre: creating incident on pagerduty, will alert sec&infra rotation runbooks.
tina-oncall: pinging legal/compliance for data exfil concerns. any sign of secret exfil?
marcos: scanning container network connections — none to external hosts except to registry during pull. no outgoing connections from container when we sampled.
elsena: good. create a timeline in the ticket with these artifacts: fs tar, layer sha, registry push metadata, KMS decrypt logs, IAM role binding diffs, CI job logs. assign to infra-sig and sec-triage.
raj: RBAC check: `kubectl get rolebinding -A | grep ci-service-account` — CI uses a minimal role for pushing to registry (artifact registry role). no cluster-admin grants found.
elsena: still could be compromised CI runner credentials (runners-redwood-5). request CI team to rotate runner tokens and audit who had access to modify pipelines.
marcos: collected attacker-sample.md with indicators: file path, mode, sha, layer id. uploading to incident ticket now.
ela­na: wait— (typo) elena: also search for other images with same layer sha.
audit-bot: registry: found same blob in 2 other internal repos (sandbox/test-payments) pulled by dev runners on 2026-01-17. tagging those images for quarantine.
elsena: good catch. notify teams owning those repos.
sara-sre: quarantined images by setting registry policy and adding temporary deny pull for sandbox projects.
tina-oncall: drafting customer-facing comms? not yet, low confidence of exfil, but this is an internal image integrity issue. will coordinate with comms if needed.
elsena: post-incident actions for tomorrow: full CI runner host audit, enforce image signing (cosign) for pipeline, add runtime policy to block suid in images at admission time, add registry webhook to alert on new suid blob.
marcos: will open GH issue in infra/ci to add cosign gating.
raj: adding kubectl commands used to the ticket for reproducibility:
```
kubectl cordon gke-payments-pool-3-7c9b
kubectl drain gke-payments-pool-3-7c9b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl scale deploy/payments-worker -n payments --replicas=0
kubectl exec -n payments payments-worker-5 -c worker -- ls -la /usr/bin/.suid_helper
```
elsena: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread. I'll file a formal incident report if we confirm CI compromise. :thumbsup:
marcos: update @1735000200 — CI team rotated runner tokens and disabled the job that pushed v1.3.4. registrar scan in progress.
sara-sre: update @1735000360 — node reimaged and returned to pool after full host audit. pods redeployed to known-good digests.
elsena: closing action list for now. follow-ups tracked in ticket IR-2026-142.
